name: Solid oxide electrolysis
applications: nuclear or industrial waste-heat coupled hydrogen
principle: A ceramic electrolyte conducts oxide ions at high temperature (650 to 850 °C according to DOE). Steam is fed to the cathode where it splits into hydrogen and oxide ions, which cross the ceramic and form oxygen at the anode. Part of the energy comes as heat, so electricity use per kilogram is lower than in low-temperature electrolysis, especially when steam comes from process heat.
